summary: Set 116 Session 2 of 3, "Close the two holes in the verification loop." HOLE 1 (the bypassed cap): `verify_session` has refused past the bounded totals since Set 111 S1, but `close_backstop` resolved a round and routed with NO bound at all -- so the cap the workflow documented did not exist on the path that runs at every close lacking stamped evidence, and router metrics show the backstop reaching rounds 5-10 (Set 111 S2), 5-12 (Set 112 S3) and 5-7 (Set 114 S1). The backstop now evaluates the SAME bound through the SAME function (`evaluate_phase_bound`, phase=None -> PHASE_BOUND_CLASSIC) before any metered call; no second budget was invented. At the cap it refuses deterministically with a new `round_bound_reached` outcome, wired into close_session's gate-failure mapping so the close BLOCKS, and the refusal names the two exits that already exist (`close_session --manual-verify`, or the operator authorizing one more round via `verify_session --operator-authorized-round`) rather than inventing a third flag. Ordering is load-bearing: the check sits AFTER the settling-evidence skip, so a session that ran a long loop and then verified clean still closes. HOLE 2 (the invisible rounds): every backstop round is now appended to `sN-rounds.jsonl` with a `source` field reusing the F3 stamp's closed producer vocabulary (STAMP_SOURCES) rather than minting a second one; the ledger path is declared as mid-close bookkeeping on BOTH the run path (`written_paths`) and the rerun-after-a-later-gate-failure path (`_settling_bookkeeping_paths` -- the I-084-S2-9 sibling, L-069-1), so it cannot trip working_tree_clean. Found and fixed a self-inflicted regression in the same pass: a mid-close ledger write would have become a `checklist_posted` transition whose "post after this" window opens after the last moment the orchestrator could post into it, failing EVERY backstop-verified close on an impossible obligation; `_checklist_transitions` now skips backstop-sourced rounds, keyed off the imported constant rather than a hardcoded token. The third route named by the spec, the discovery fan-out, was already inside the budget (K parallel calls = one round) -- that property is now asserted by tests rather than merely true. STALENESS REGRESSION (spec step 4): pinned end-to-end at the level the bug actually bit -- a passed round plus a recorded final test run still settles the close with zero fresh metered rounds -- paired with a look-alike proving the exemption stays narrow (real work landing after the round still stales it). TESTS: 15 new (12 in test_close_backstop.py, 3 in test_verify_session_phases.py), each rule pinned from both sides per L-112-1: the planted violation that must refuse AND the legitimate look-alike that must not. One fixture bug was caught and fixed during authoring -- it passed alone and failed under parallel load because it depended on Windows' ~15.6ms clock resolution being too COARSE to separate a checklist post from the rounds seeded after it; the honest fix was to post after each seeded round as the real cadence requires, not to loosen the assertion. VERIFICATION: round 1 discovery, 2-lens fan-out (spec-conformance + failure-scenario), both lenses VERIFIED, ZERO Critical/Major, $0.78, anthropic correctly excluded. Eight nits total; two were factual errors in records this session wrote (a wrong test count of 18 vs the true 15, and a missing sessionNumber) and were FIXED; three substantive ones are recorded as adjudicated-minor residuals in blockers[] with reasoning, journaled in decisions.jsonl under `defer-to-existing-gate`. SUITES: full pytest after freeze 3829 passed / 5 skipped in 255.58s (4:15, parallel), and full Layer 3 Playwright 36 passed in 11.7m -- owed because close_session.py is on the playwright suite's covers list as a blessed state-file writer.

reason.specifics: Session 3 implements the operator's gate ruling (ten checks to three gates plus two transactional preconditions plus five demotions) and must not quietly convert a demotion into a deletion. It also depends directly on this session's staleness fix for its Step 5 -> Step 8 reordering of the full-suite run, and it will edit `test_run_fresh`'s scoping in run_of_record.py -- the same freshness machinery Session 2 just regression-tested. Same orchestrator keeps that context. Session 3 additionally owes the REQUIRED end-of-set path-aware critique and change-log.md.

blockers: ADJUDICATED-MINOR RESIDUAL 1 of 3 (round 1, lens 2 -- failure-scenario): a backstop attempt that dies in TRANSPORT is never ledgered. `record_round_completed` runs only after routing, parsing and classification succeed, so a `route_failed` / `verification_unavailable` return, or an interruption before the append, leaves the bound unchanged. ADJUDICATION: correct as designed, not a hole. It matches `verify_session`, which also records only rounds that produced a verdict, and it is the right semantics -- a round that returned nothing should not consume a budget meant to bound REVIEW cycles. The spend is still audited: the billable call is in router-metrics.jsonl either way. RESIDUAL OWNER: none required; re-raise only if a session is observed burning repeated failed backstop attempts.

ADJUDICATED-MINOR RESIDUAL 2 of 3 (round 1, lens 2): round NUMBERING still comes from the artifacts on disk (`resolve_round`), not from the ledger, so deleting or losing canonical artifacts could duplicate a round number and bypass ledger-based totals. ADJUDICATION: pre-existing Set 111 S1 behaviour, neither introduced nor worsened here; the bound itself already counts the UNION of the ledger and the findings envelopes precisely so neither source alone is load-bearing. The claim it strains is a wording one -- 'the ledger is the true count' means the true count of rounds RUN (the backstop's were previously absent entirely), not that the ledger allocates round numbers. RESIDUAL OWNER: a future set that makes the ledger authoritative for numbering as well as counting; it would want its own falsifier (delete an artifact, assert the round number does not regress).

ADJUDICATED-MINOR RESIDUAL 3 of 3 (round 1, lens 2) -- THE ONE WORTH FIXING: `_round_bound_remediation()` interpolates the session-set dir into a copy-pasteable `verify_session` command without quoting, so a repo path containing spaces yields a command the operator must repair by hand -- at exactly the moment they are blocked. ADJUDICATION: real but Minor, and deliberately NOT point-fixed, because it is a pre-existing CLASS: `verify_session`'s own past-the-bound refusal message and `gate_checks._verify_session_command` interpolate the same path the same unquoted way. Fixing only the site this session added would leave the class alive while the changelog read as though it were closed (L-069-1 forbids exactly that), and fixing all three mid-close would expand scope past the plan and buy a re-verification round for a nit. RESIDUAL OWNER: a small scoped follow-on covering all three sites at once, whose tests plant a spaced path and assert the emitted command survives it. This repo's own path has no spaces, so it is latent here.

PROCESS NOTE (not a defect, recorded so the next session does not repeat it): running the Layer 3 Playwright suite CONCURRENTLY with the verification round cost a second metered verification. Playwright's build rebuilt `tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/dist/`, those rebuilt files were bound into the round's freshness stamp, and reverting the rebuild -- correct, since this session touched no extension source -- changed the work-diff digest and staled the stamp. The close backstop therefore ran its own round over the final tree. That is the sanctioned path and it dogfooded this session's change end to end (bound evaluated, round ledgered with `source: close_session_backstop`), but the cheaper ordering is to run Layer 3 BEFORE verification, not beside it.

SCOPE NOTE: two files outside the spec's Touches list were edited, both as necessary consequences of the named change rather than scope creep -- `ai_router/close_session.py` (the new backstop status must be mapped to a gate failure or the refusal would silently pass the close) and `ai_router/gate_checks.py` (without the checklist-transition skip, the new ledger write would fail every backstop-verified close). Surfaced here for the Step 9 review.
